title: Alcohol DUI causing injury
summary: Driving under the influence of alcohol, while concurrently committing an unlawful act or neglecting a legal driving duty that proximately causes bodily injury to someone other than the driver. Impairment or the charged blood-alcohol level alone is insufficient without the additional act/duty breach and causal injury.
penalty: Misdemeanor or felony. Ordinary first-offense punishment under section 23554 is 90 days to 364 days in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison, AND a $390-$1,000 base fine. First-offense probation under 23556 instead requires at least 5 days in jail, the fine and applicable programs. One qualifying prior offense within 10 years under 23560 raises the ordinary county-jail minimum to 120 days and the fine range to $390-$5,000; 23562 has separate probation/program alternatives, including a 30-day minimum under its specified program route. Two or more qualifying prior offenses within 10 years under 23566 ordinarily require 2, 3 or 4 years in state prison and a $1,015-$5,000 fine; 23568 governs available probation alternatives. Specified prior felony DUI or manslaughter convictions may independently invoke 23550.5. License suspension/revocation and separate injury or multiple-victim enhancements may apply; a generic prior-conviction answer is insufficient to assign a higher tier. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution, probation and administrative licensing consequences require separate review.
mentalState: Voluntary driving with the charged impairment or blood-alcohol condition, concurrent unlawful conduct or neglected duty, and proximate injury causation.

title: Driving a commercial vehicle with blood alcohol of 0.04 percent or more
summary: Driving a commercial motor vehicle as defined in section 15210 with blood alcohol of 0.04 percent or more. A qualifying test within three hours creates a rebuttable presumption. The statutory commercial-vehicle definition controls; a vehicle is not commercial solely because driving is work-related.
penalty: Ordinarily a misdemeanor. First offense under 23536: 96 hours to 6 months in county jail AND a $390-$1,000 base fine; first-offense probation under 23538 has distinct program and custody conditions. A qualifying prior within 10 years can require 90 days to 364 days in jail under 23540, and two qualifying priors can require 120 days to 364 days under 23546, with the $390-$1,000 fine. Sections 23542 and 23548 govern their separate probation/program alternatives. Three or more qualifying priors within 10 years under 23550 can permit 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison or 180 days to 364 days in county jail, plus the fine. Specified prior felony DUI or manslaughter convictions can independently invoke 23550.5, which permits state prison or up to 364 days in jail plus the fine. Suspension/revocation, treatment and interlock requirements depend on the case; no generic prior-conviction answer establishes a felony branch. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution, probation and administrative licensing consequences require separate review.
mentalState: Voluntary driving with the charged blood-alcohol level and commercial-vehicle or actual paying-passenger condition.

title: Driving with a license suspended for reckless or negligent operation
summary: Knowingly driving while the driving privilege is suspended or revoked for a reason specifically listed in 14601(a), including reckless driving, listed refusal grounds, or negligent/incompetent operation. Other suspension reasons use different statutes. The limited employer/private-property exception and its offstreet-parking exclusion must be checked.
penalty: Misdemeanor: first conviction, 5 days to 6 months in county jail AND a $300-$1,000 fine. If the offense occurs within five years of a qualifying prior offense resulting in conviction under 14601, 14601.1, 14601.2 or 14601.5: 10 days to 364 days AND a $500-$2,000 fine; probation requires at least 10 days. A qualifying plea substitution for 14601.2 can trigger ignition-interlock requirements. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution, probation and administrative licensing consequences require separate review.
mentalState: Knowledge of the suspension, revocation or restriction and driving in violation of it. Statutory notice provisions do not replace the prosecution's obligation to prove knowledge; the source's conclusive-presumption wording is not presented as automatic guilt.

title: Driving with a license suspended for other reasons
summary: Knowingly driving while suspended or revoked for a reason outside 14601, 14601.2 and 14601.5. The limited employer/private-property exception must be checked. The source excludes an offstreet parking facility but cites 12500(d); the retained definition is in 12500(c). This apparent cross-reference discrepancy is preserved and flagged, not silently corrected.
penalty: Misdemeanor or infraction under Penal Code sections 17(d) and 19.8. Misdemeanor first conviction: up to 6 months in county jail, a $300-$1,000 fine, or both. If the offense occurs within five years of a qualifying prior offense resulting in conviction under the listed suspension statutes: 5 days to 364 days AND a $500-$2,000 fine. If handled as an infraction, there is no incarceration and the fine is up to $250. A qualifying plea substitution for 14601.2 can trigger interlock requirements; the filing and disposition must be confirmed. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution, probation and administrative licensing consequences require separate review.

title: Driving after a DUI license suspension or revocation
summary: Knowingly driving while suspended or revoked for a conviction under 23152 or 23153. The limited employer/private-property rehabilitation exception and applicable off-highway operation must be checked.
penalty: Misdemeanor: first conviction, 10 days to 6 months in county jail AND a $300-$1,000 fine; probation requires at least 10 days. A qualifying prior offense within five years raises this to 30 days to 364 days AND a $500-$2,000 fine, with at least 30 days on probation. A qualifying second/subsequent offense over five but within seven years can require at least 10 days as a probation condition. A qualifying habitual-traffic-offender designation can additionally require 180 days and a $2,000 fine under 14601.3(e)(3). Interlock and reinstatement rules apply under the governing 23573/23575 scheme; the correct scheme and eligibility must be checked. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution, probation and administrative licensing consequences require separate review.

title: Reckless driving causing bodily injury
summary: Reckless driving that proximately causes bodily injury to someone other than the driver, subject to the separate higher branches in 23104(b) and 23105. An accident or ordinary negligence alone is not reckless driving.
penalty: Ordinary misdemeanor under 23104(a): 30 days to 6 months in county jail, a $220-$1,000 fine, or both. The qualifying-prior/great-bodily-injury branch in 23104(b), and the specified-injury branch in 23105, have separate misdemeanor/felony alternatives and must not be assigned this ordinary penalty. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution, probation and administrative licensing consequences require separate review.

title: Reckless driving causing great bodily injury with a qualifying prior

penalty: Misdemeanor or felony: 30 days to 6 months in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under Penal Code 1170(h); a $220-$1,000 fine may be imposed alone or with imprisonment. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution, probation and administrative licensing consequences require separate review.

title: Motor vehicle speed contest
summary: Engaging in a motor-vehicle speed contest on a highway or an offstreet parking facility, including racing another vehicle or a timing device. The statutory lawful-speed event over a route longer than 20 miles is excluded. Merely watching an event is not this driving offense.
penalty: Ordinary misdemeanor under 23109(e)(1): 24 hours to 90 days in county jail, a $355-$1,000 fine, or both, plus 40 hours of community service. Causing another person bodily injury raises the ordinary range to 30 days to 6 months, a $500-$1,000 fine, or both under (e)(2). A qualifying repeat within five years under (f) carries custody AND fine; its serious-bodily-injury branch permits 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison or 30 days to 364 days in county jail, AND a $500-$1,000 fine. Repeat probation under (g) has a separate minimum of 48 hours. Specified injuries also support the separate 23109.1 choice. License suspension/restriction, community-service and impound consequences depend on the branch. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution, probation and administrative licensing consequences require separate review.

title: Failure to present a driver license on lawful demand
summary: A driver fails to present the driver license for examination on demand of a peace officer enforcing the Vehicle Code. This is distinct from subdivision (a), which concerns carrying the license and has a production-in-court dismissal rule.
penalty: Misdemeanor under section 40000.11, with the default punishment in 42002: up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. title: Failure to appear on a written traffic promise
summary: Willfully violating a written promise to appear in court or before an authorized bail-deposit recipient, including a lawfully granted continuance.
